title: Phosphate Transporter Gene Expression (Pht1 Family) and Arbuscular Mycorrhizal Symbiosis
description: Doctoral research on high inorganic P (H2PO4-) suppression of mycorrhizal colonization, Pht1 transporter expression kinetics, and strigolactone root exudate signaling.
image_caption: Microscopic view of fungal arbuscules inside root cortical cells under mycorrhizal inoculation.
overview: Arbuscular Mycorrhizal Fungi (AMF, e.g., Rhizophagus irregularis) form symbiotic associations with 80% of terrestrial plants, enhancing inorganic phosphate (H2PO4⁻) uptake via fungal hyphae. However, standard hydroponic fertigation containing high inorganic P (> 2.0 mM) down-regulates root strigolactone exudation and represses the mycorrhiza-specific phosphate transporter gene SlPT4. This paper formulates a precision P-dosing threshold ([H2PO4⁻] = 0.35 mM) that maintains 78% AMF root colonization while sustaining maximal plant biomass growth.

climate_strategy.strategy: Inoculate organic coconut coir substrate with Rhizophagus irregularis spores at seeding. Restrict initial fertigation Monopotassium Phosphate [PubChem CID 516951] to 0.3 mM during the first 4 weeks to induce symbiosis establishment.

crop_steering.intro: Biological symbiosis steering matrix for organic hydroponic production.

generative_triggers.irrigation: Inorganic P: 0.80 mM (Maintenance Phase via Fungal Hyphae)

fertigation.intro: Nutrient solution formulation for mycorrhizal compatibility.
fertigation.vegetative_phase: Dose Monopotassium Phosphate [PubChem CID 516951] at 0.35 mM (P 11 mg/L) combined with Organic Nitrogen sources to prevent fungal hyphal inhibition.
fertigation.generative_phase: Supplement Potassium Nitrate [PubChem CID 24434] (K 4.5 mM) to meet potassium demand without overloading phosphate ions.

references.text: Phosphate availability regulates mycorrhizal symbiosis and Pht1 gene expression in horticultural crops.
